Post Copy (280 char max): A knockout mouse has a gene completely turned off. No expression. No protein. Just clean loss of function. We've built 2,500+ since 1998. #KnockoutMice #GeneTargeting
Conventional knockouts delete a gene globally, in every cell. Simple and powerful, unless that gene is essential for development. Then you need a different strategy. #KnockoutMice
What if you could delete a gene in only one tissue? Conditional knockouts using Cre lox give you that control. No embryonic lethality. Clean, targeted deletion. #ConditionalKO
Two loxP sites flanking your exon. Cross with a Cre driver. Gene deleted only where Cre is expressed. Liver, brain, T cells, you choose. #ConditionalKO #CreLox
TruView is a reporter AND a conditional knockout in one allele. Before Cre: see where the gene is active. After Cre: study the loss of function. Two experiments, one mouse. #TruView
Some genes are too important during development to knock out early. Inducible conditional knockouts let the mouse grow up healthy first. You pick when deletion happens. #InducibleKO
Deleting a gene everywhere tells you it matters. Deleting it in one tissue tells you WHERE it matters. That's the power of tissue specific knockouts. #TissueSpecific #CreLox
How do you confirm your conditional knockout worked in the right cells? Build a reporter into the allele. When Cre deletes the gene, the reporter turns on. Confirmation built in. #CreLox
One allele, four possible models. The knockout first design starts as a null but converts to a conditional, a reporter, or a floxed line with strategic recombination. #KnockoutFirst
Global or conditional? It's the first decision in any knockout project. Global is faster. Conditional gives tissue and temporal control. The right choice depends on your gene. #Knockout
Knockouts remove genes. Knockins add something new: a human gene, a reporter, a point mutation, a tag. It's how you humanize targets and model patient mutations. #KnockinMice
Want human protein expressed from the mouse locus? A cDNA knockin replaces the mouse coding sequence with human cDNA. Physiological levels, right tissues, no overexpression artifacts. #cDNA
One nucleotide. One amino acid. That's often the difference between healthy and diseased. Point mutation models recreate the exact variants found in human patients. #PointMutation
Where is your gene expressed? In which cells? Reporter knockins insert GFP or LacZ under your gene's promoter. Everywhere it would be active, the reporter lights up. #ReporterMice
Can't find a good antibody for your protein? Tag it at the endogenous locus. FLAG, HA, V5. Native regulation, tagged protein, well characterized commercial antibodies. #EpitopeTag
FLAG tags are small, reliable, and have great commercial antibodies. A FLAG knockin at the endogenous locus means native expression with detection that actually works. #FLAGTag
Nine amino acids. That's all an HA tag adds. But now your protein is detectable with high affinity validated antibodies for IP, western, ChIP, and IF. Small tag, big capability. #HATag
GFP knockins let you see gene expression in real time. No staining, no secondary antibodies. Every cell that expresses your gene glows green. Live imaging, FACS, lineage tracing. #GFP
tdTomato is roughly 6x brighter than EGFP. That matters when you're imaging deep tissue or sorting rare cell populations. Brighter reporter, better data. #tdTomato #Fluorescence
LacZ has been the gold standard reporter for decades. X gal staining is cheap, simple, and gives you whole mount visualization. No confocal required. Sometimes classics win. #LacZ
A conditional knockin stays silent until Cre removes a STOP cassette. You control where and when the inserted gene turns on. Perfect for gain of function and oncogene studies. #Knockin
Mouse proteins don't always respond to human drugs. Humanized mice replace mouse genes with human counterparts so your therapeutic binds its actual target in vivo. #HumanizedMice
Gene replacement is the most complete humanization. The full human gene, exons, introns, regulatory elements, sitting in the mouse genome. Human protein, physiological regulation. #Humanized
P53 is mutated in over half of all human cancers. A p53 humanized mouse carries human TP53, letting you study patient specific variants and test p53 reactivating compounds. #P53 #Oncology
Checkpoint immunotherapy doesn't work in wild type mice. Human inhibitors need human targets. Checkpoint humanized mice express human PD1, PDL1, CTLA4, LAG3, or TIM3. #IO
Pembrolizumab, nivolumab, cemiplimab. Every anti PD1 drug targets HUMAN PD1. A PD1 humanized mouse expresses human PD1 on its T cells in a fully immunocompetent host. #PD1 #Immunotherapy
PDL1 is the target of atezolizumab, durvalumab, and avelumab. Test human anti PDL1 therapeutics in vivo with a functioning immune system and a human target on the tumor. #PDL1 #IO
CTLA4 was the first immune checkpoint ever targeted therapeutically. Ipilimumab changed oncology. Testing anti CTLA4 antibodies requires a model expressing human CTLA4. #CTLA4
LAG3 is the next wave of checkpoint immunotherapy. Multiple anti LAG3 antibodies are in trials, often combined with anti PD1. You need models expressing human LAG3. #LAG3 #IO
TIM3 plays unique roles in T cell exhaustion that other checkpoints don't cover. Testing human anti TIM3 agents requires a mouse expressing human TIM3. Stay ahead of the wave. #TIM3
Your drug targets a human receptor. Your mouse has the mouse version with different binding kinetics and epitopes. Receptor humanized mice fix that mismatch. #Humanized #Preclinical
Human cytokines don't always signal through mouse receptors the same way. That mismatch gives you misleading preclinical data. Cytokine humanized mice solve this. #Cytokine #Humanized
Some projects can't wait 12 months. F.A.S.T. technology skips chimera breeding entirely, going straight from ES cells to fully ES cell derived mice. Same precision, faster timeline. #FAST
Some genes are too big for standard vectors. BAC based targeting handles insertions of 50kb, 100kb, even 200kb+. When your project outgrows conventional approaches. #BAC #GeneTargeting
Random insertion transgenics are unpredictable. Targeted transgenics go into a safe harbor locus. Guaranteed expression, consistent levels, no position effects. #Transgenics #SafeHarbor
A safe harbor locus lets you insert any transgene and get reliable expression without disrupting endogenous genes. Rosa26, HPRT, H11. Each with different advantages. #SafeHarbor
Rosa26 is the most widely used safe harbor in mouse genetics. Ubiquitous expression, tolerates large insertions, doesn't disrupt development. Thousands of published models use it. #Rosa26
Standard Rosa26 works. Rapid Rosa26 works faster. Pre characterized ES cells with the locus already targeted. Insert your transgene, compress the timeline. Same locus, fewer steps. #Rosa26
HPRT offers something Rosa26 doesn't: built in positive and negative selection. Easier to identify correctly targeted clones. A powerful safe harbor alternative. #HPRT #SafeHarbor
H11 is the newest safe harbor gaining traction. Strong ubiquitous expression like Rosa26 but at an independent locus. When Rosa26 is occupied, H11 gives you a second site. #H11
Not every project needs a custom build. Over 10,000 pre engineered mouse and rat models ready to go. Knockouts, knockins, reporters, Cre drivers, humanized checkpoints. Browse first. #Catalog
Off the shelf humanized models with human genes already integrated. Characterized, ready to breed, available now. Check the catalog before commissioning a custom build. #HumanizedMice
Single AND double humanized immune checkpoint models in the catalog. PD1/CTLA4, PD1/LAG3, PD1/TIM3 combinations ready for immuno oncology studies. No custom build wait. #IO #Catalog
Building a conditional knockout? You need a Cre driver for your tissue of interest. Our catalog has lines for major tissues and cell types ready to cross with your floxed model. #CreDriver
GFP, tdTomato, LacZ reporters ready to ship. Standalone or Rosa26 targeted, ready for Cre activation. Off the shelf, validated, ready to breed. #ReporterMice #Catalog
Cancer research needs models as complex as the disease. Tumor suppressor knockouts, oncogene activation, syngeneic backgrounds, humanized checkpoints. 26 years of building them. #Oncology
P53, BRCA1, RB1, APC, PTEN. Every major tumor suppressor has been studied using knockout mice. Model cancer initiation at the genetic level. #TumorSuppressor #Oncology
Tumor suppressors prevent cancer. Oncogenes drive it. Conditional knockins keep the oncogene silent until Cre activates it in a specific tissue. Controlled cancer on your timeline. #Oncogene
Immunotherapy testing needs an intact immune system. Syngeneic models use mouse cancer cells in immunocompetent hosts. The immune response is real. The workhorse of IO research. #Syngeneic
IO is where immunology meets cancer. You need intact immune systems, humanized checkpoints, and syngeneic backgrounds. Getting the model wrong means your drug never had a fair test. #IO
Your compound works in vitro. Now what? Cancer drug efficacy models test dosing, scheduling, and response in vivo with the target, tumor microenvironment, and immune system all present. #Oncology
Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, ALS, Huntington's, epilepsy, autism. Each neurological disease requires models with specific mutations, expression patterns, and behavioral phenotypes. #Neuroscience
APP, PSEN1, MAPT, TREM2, APOE. Alzheimer's research depends on mice carrying the same mutations found in patients. The model you choose determines which pathology you can study. #Alzheimers
Alpha synuclein aggregation. Dopaminergic neuron loss. Motor dysfunction. Parkinson's models recreate these hallmarks using knockins of human SNCA mutations. #Parkinsons #Neuroscience
Huntington's is caused by a CAG repeat expansion in HTT. The length determines severity. Mouse models carry humanized HTT with expanded repeats. Genetics drives the design. #Huntingtons
SOD1, TDP43, FUS, C9orf72. ALS is genetically diverse and each gene produces different pathology. Match your model to your drug's mechanism of action. #ALS #MotorNeuron
Seizures from ion channel dysfunction. SCN1A, KCNQ2, GABRA1 knockouts and knockins that shift excitation and inhibition. Genetic models produce spontaneous, not just induced seizures. #Epilepsy
Autism isn't one disease. It's hundreds of variants converging on behavior. SHANK3, MECP2, FMR1, CNTNAP2 models help researchers understand which pathways drive which symptoms. #Autism

Genetic models targeting serotonin transporters, BDNF, and CRF receptors produce measurable behavioral phenotypes that respond to pharmacological intervention. Better models, better drugs. #Psychiatry
Diabetes, obesity, NASH, lipid disorders. Metabolic disease is a global epidemic. Custom knockouts, knockins, and humanized models targeting metabolic pathways. #MetabolicDisease #Preclinical
Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes have completely different pathologies and need different mouse models. T1D: autoimmune beta cell destruction. T2D: insulin resistance. One name, two diseases. #Diabetes
T1D is autoimmune. The immune system destroys insulin producing beta cells. Models need to capture immune mediated destruction, not just elevated blood glucose. #Type1Diabetes
Insulin resistance, hyperglycemia, beta cell failure, obesity. T2D models need to recapitulate the metabolic syndrome, not just one symptom. Complex disease, complex models. #Type2Diabetes
Leptin, melanocortin, ghrelin, NPY, POMC. Obesity is driven by dozens of pathways. The right model depends on which one your therapeutic targets. Match the model to the mechanism. #Obesity
NASH (now MASH) is the leading cause of liver transplant with no approved drug. The race for therapeutics needs models that develop steatosis, inflammation, fibrosis, and ballooning. #NASH
Cholesterol, triglycerides, PCSK9, LDLR, APOE. Lipid metabolism models are essential for cardiovascular drug discovery and understanding how genetic variants affect circulating lipids. #Lipids
Metabolic syndrome isn't one disease. Obesity, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, hypertension all converging. Modeling it requires genetics that produce multiple phenotypes simultaneously. #MetSyn
The immune system is the most complex network in the body. Autoimmunity, inflammation, allergy, IBD, lupus, RA. Each disorder has specific genetic drivers and model requirements. #Immunology
When the immune system attacks self. Models targeting CTLA4, Foxp3, AIRE, or specific TCR sequences drive self reactive responses. Understanding tolerance requires genetic precision. #Autoimmune
Chronic inflammation drives tissue damage in dozens of diseases. Models targeting TNF, IL6, IL1B, and NFkB let you dissect which signals matter and test anti inflammatory therapeutics. #Inflammation
Allergic airway inflammation, IgE overproduction, mast cell degranulation. Asthma models need genetics that recapitulate the Th2 skewed immune response seen in patients. #Asthma #Allergy
Crohn's and ulcerative colitis affect millions. IBD models target barrier function, immune regulation, and microbiome interaction. IL10 knockouts, NOD2 mutants, T cell transfer. #IBD #Colitis
Lupus attacks virtually every organ. Models targeting Fas, complement, and TLR signaling produce autoantibodies, immune complex deposition, and the multi system pathology seen in SLE. #Lupus
Joint inflammation, cartilage destruction, bone erosion. RA models targeting TNF, IL6, and T cell signaling produce arthritis that responds to the same biologics used in patients. #RA
Heart disease is the number one killer globally. Atherosclerosis, heart failure, hypertension, fibrosis. Each requires targeted genetic modifications to produce relevant pathology. #Cardio
LDLR knockout, APOE knockout, PCSK9 overexpression. The workhorses of atherosclerosis research. Plaques on high fat diets that respond to lipid lowering interventions. #Atherosclerosis
Modeling heart failure requires genetic approaches producing cardiac dysfunction, not just hypertrophy. Conditional knockouts in cardiomyocytes with translational relevance. #HeartFailure
Blood pressure involves kidneys, vasculature, nervous system, and endocrine. Hypertension models target renin angiotensin, endothelial NO, and sodium handling pathways. #Hypertension
Fibrosis is where heart disease gets irreversible. Collagen replaces functional myocardium. Models targeting TGF beta and fibroblast activation produce progressive cardiac fibrosis. #Fibrosis
Over 7,000 rare diseases. Most are genetic. Most have no treatment. Mouse models are often the only preclinical tool available. Every rare disease deserves a research model. #RareDisease
Gaucher's, Fabry's, Pompe, Tay Sachs. Enzyme deficiencies causing toxic substrate accumulation. Mouse models with the same mutations develop progressive multi organ pathology. #LSD #RareDisease
Duchenne, Becker, limb girdle. Progressive muscle wasting from mutations in dystrophin and structural muscle proteins. Essential for testing gene therapy and exon skipping. #MuscularDystrophy
CFTR is one gene but mutations produce disease across lungs, pancreas, liver, and intestines. CF models carry specific mutations like F508del for therapeutic testing. #CysticFibrosis
Orphan diseases each affect fewer than 200,000 people. But collectively, 30 million Americans. A custom mouse model is often the only preclinical tool that exists. #OrphanDisease
The eye is one of the most accessible organs for gene therapy. Retinal degeneration, glaucoma, macular degeneration. Each needs models with specific genetic modifications. #Ophthalmology
Photoreceptor degeneration, RPE dysfunction, ganglion cell death. Retinal models carry rhodopsin, RPE65, or CRB1 mutations and develop progressive vision loss. #RetinalDisease
Glaucoma: leading cause of irreversible blindness. Models targeting aqueous humor dynamics and RGC survival produce measurable IOP elevation and ganglion cell loss. #Glaucoma
AMD is the leading cause of vision loss in adults over 60. Models targeting complement factors, VEGF signaling, and RPE biology produce drusen and neovascularization. #AMD #MacularDegeneration
There's more than one way to engineer a mouse genome. ES cell targeting, homologous recombination, selection cassettes. The right technology depends on your allele design. #GeneTargeting
ES cell targeting lets you characterize the allele BEFORE making the mouse. You know it's correct before investing in germline transmission. That's pre germline QC. #ESCells #GeneTargeting
Southern blot confirmation, karyotype analysis, junction sequencing. All done on the ES cell clone before a single blastocyst is injected. QC that other approaches can't match. #ESCells
Most gene targeting failures are found AFTER mouse generation. Pre germline characterization catches problems at the ES cell stage, before months of wasted breeding. #PreGermline #QC
A correctly targeted ES cell clone is the foundation of your entire model. We characterize every clone by Southern blot, PCR, and sequencing before proceeding. No shortcuts. #ESCells
Homologous recombination uses the cell's own DNA repair to swap engineered sequence into the exact location you want. No random insertion. No off targets. Precise and site specific. #GeneTargeting
Every targeting vector needs a selection cassette. Neo or hygromycin? Flanked by FRT or loxP? Self excising or removable by breeding? The details shape your final allele. #SelectionCassette
Neomycin resistance is the most common selection marker in gene targeting. G418 kills untargeted cells. Flank with FRT sites for clean removal later. #Neomycin #GeneTargeting
Already using Neo in your line? Hygromycin gives you a second selectable marker. Essential for sequential targeting when you need to modify a second allele. Two markers, one clone. #Hygromycin
Traditional cassettes need a Cre or FLP cross to remove. Self excising cassettes remove themselves during germline transmission. No extra crosses. Weeks saved. #SelfExcising #GeneTargeting
Conditional targeting gives you control that global modifications can't. Delete in one tissue. Activate at one timepoint. Cre lox, FLP FRT, and inducible systems make it possible. #Conditional
Two loxP sites. One Cre enzyme. Delete, invert, or activate any DNA sequence between them. The backbone of conditional genetics for three decades. Elegant, reliable, proven. #CreLox
Where you place loxP sites determines everything. Too close to the exon? Disrupted splicing. Wrong orientation? Inversion instead of deletion. Placement is an art backed by data. #loxP
Your floxed mouse is half the equation. Cre drivers express Cre in specific tissues: Albumin for liver, Nestin for brain, LysM for macrophages. The driver determines WHERE it happens. #Cre
Hepatocytes, cardiomyocytes, podocytes, osteoblasts, adipocytes. Hundreds of Cre lines exist, each driving recombination in a defined cell population. Choose the right one. #CreLines
FLP FRT is the second major recombination system. FLP recognizes FRT sites like Cre recognizes loxP. Use it for a second layer of control independent of Cre. Two switches, one mouse. #FLPFRT
Cre lox. FLP FRT. Now Dre Rox. A third orthogonal recombination system. Dre recognizes Rox sites without cross reacting with loxP or FRT. Triple recombinase models are now possible. #DreRox
Constitutive expression starts at conception. Inducible starts when you decide. Turn genes on or off at any point in the mouse's life. Temporal control changes what you can study. #Inducible
CreERT2 sits dormant until tamoxifen. Then it enters the nucleus and cuts at loxP sites. You choose when. Days, weeks, or months after birth. Timing is everything. #Tamoxifen #CreERT2
Dox in the water, gene turns on. Remove dox, gene turns off. Unlike tamoxifen Cre (permanent), doxycycline systems are reversible. When you need to turn a gene on AND off. #Doxycycline
Tet On: add dox, gene activates. Tet Off: remove dox, gene activates. Same drug, opposite logic. Both are reversible and dose responsive with decades of validation. #TetSystem
The allele is the blueprint. Every loxP site, FRT site, cassette, and exon boundary must be designed up front. Good design anticipates derivative alleles and downstream needs. #AlleleDesign
One targeted allele. Four mouse models. The derivative system (tm1a, tm1b, tm1c, tm1d) converts a single knockout first allele into a null, conditional, or reporter. Maximum flexibility. #Derivatives
The tm1a allele is where it starts. Knockout first with a LacZ reporter and floxed exon. Default: null. Apply FLP: conditional (tm1c). Apply Cre: complete null (tm1b). One clone, three options. #tm1a
tm1b is what you get when Cre removes the floxed exon and cassette from tm1a. Clean null allele with LacZ reporter still active. Gene deleted, loss of function confirmed visually. #tm1b
tm1c is the conditional ready version. FLP removes the gene trap from tm1a, leaving a floxed critical exon. Cross with any Cre driver for tissue specific deletion (tm1d). #tm1c #Floxed
tm1d: tissue specific deletion of the critical exon from a tm1c floxed allele. Cre removes the exon in your tissue of choice. Null in that tissue, normal everywhere else. #tm1d
Which exon do you delete? It must be in all splice variants, disrupt reading frame when removed, and be large enough to prevent skipping. Get it wrong and you might still have protein. #ExonSelection
Deleting an exon doesn't guarantee a null. If remaining exons stay in frame, you could get a truncated protein with partial function. Frame analysis during allele design prevents this. #ReadingFrame
C57BL/6, BALB/c, 129, FVB. Each strain has different baseline biology, immune responses, and behavior. Choose the wrong background and you might miss your phenotype entirely. #StrainBackground
C57BL/6 is the most used inbred strain and the reference genome. Well characterized biology, extensive published data, compatible with most Cre drivers. When in doubt, BL/6 is the answer. #C57BL6
Both are C57BL/6 but J and N are NOT the same. BL/6J has a natural Nnt mutation affecting glucose metabolism and redox. Mix them up and your metabolic data won't make sense. #BL6J #BL6N
BALB/c has a Th2 biased immune response. The preferred strain for immunology, allergy, and antibody production studies. Strain choice shapes your phenotype. #BALBc #Immunology
The 129 strain is where the first ES cell lines came from. 129 ES cells target with high efficiency, making it the original workhorse for homologous recombination. #129Strain #ESCells
FVB mice have large pronuclei, making them preferred for pronuclear injection transgenics. They breed well, have large litters, and are albino for imaging. #FVB #Transgenics

Many knockouts start on mixed 129/BL6 background. That genetic variability can affect your phenotype. Two mice with the same knockout but different flanking alleles, different results. #MixedBackground
Ten generations to congenic. Or speed backcross with marker assisted selection in five. Same genetic purity, half the time. Clean up your mixed background model. #Backcrossing #Congenic
Before your drug enters the clinic, prove the target matters. Knockouts, conditional KOs, and humanized knockins confirm that modulating your target works in vivo. #TargetValidation
Your compound works in cells. Does it work in a living animal? Efficacy models measure drug response with the target, disease pathology, and immune system all present. #EfficacyTesting
How fast does your drug reach the target? How long does it stay? What concentration works? PK/PD in mouse models defines parameters that shape clinical development. #PKPD #Preclinical
Safety first. Humanized models are key for tox because drugs designed for human targets might not show toxicity in wild type mice. Right target, right species. #Toxicology #DrugSafety
Biomarkers make or break clinical trials. Mouse models with well characterized disease let you identify molecular changes tracking with pathology. Better biomarkers, better trials. #Biomarker
What does this gene do? Knock it out. Observe what changes. That simple logic has driven thousands of discoveries. Gene function studies are where basic science begins. #GeneFunction
Genes work in pathways, not isolation. Double knockouts and combinatorial allele strategies let you dissect signaling cascades in vivo. Turn off one node, see what happens. #PathwayAnalysis
Where is your protein? Which cells? Which compartment? Reporter knockins and epitope tags let you see it at endogenous levels. No overexpression, no artifacts. #ProteinLocalization
Where did this cell come from? What did it become? Inducible Cre plus reporter alleles permanently mark a cell and all its descendants. Track cell fate across development or disease. #LineageTracing
Stem cells differentiate. Progenitors commit. Sometimes cells dedifferentiate. Genetic labeling tracks these transitions in vivo. Reveal which stem cells produce which tissues. #CellFateMapping
Most monoclonal antibodies target human proteins that don't exist in wild type mice. Humanized target models let you test your antibody against its actual target in vivo. #Antibody #Biologics
AAV, LNPs, base editing, prime editing. Every gene therapy needs a mouse model for efficacy, biodistribution, and safety. Disease models with the exact mutation you're correcting. #GeneTherapy
CAR T, NK cells, engineered Tregs, TIL therapy. Cell therapies need models where transferred cells can engraft, expand, and function. Immunodeficient or syngeneic backgrounds. #CellTherapy
Small molecules are still the backbone of pharma. The key is matching model to mechanism. A kinase inhibitor needs a model where that kinase drives pathology. Right model, right data. #SmallMolecule
ASOs, siRNA, miRNA. Oligo drugs target RNA, so your mouse needs the same RNA sequences. Humanized models carrying the human target gene are essential for oligo testing. #ASO #RNATherapeutics
Sometimes a mouse isn't enough. Rats offer larger size for surgery, more blood volume, and different behavioral phenotypes. Custom knockout, knockin, and transgenic rats available. #RatModels
Knockout rats let you study gene function in a larger rodent. Preferred for cardiovascular, neurobehavioral, and pharmacology studies where body size matters. #KnockoutRat #Preclinical
Humanized targets, disease mutations, reporter genes. Everything you can knock into a mouse, you can knock into a rat. When your study requires rat physiology and size. #KnockinRat
Transgenic rats with overexpressed genes, reporters, or Cre drivers expand what's possible in rat research. Neuroscience, cardiovascular physiology, and beyond. #TransgenicRat
Rabbits are preferred for antibody generation, reproductive biology, and certain cardiovascular studies. Custom gene targeted rabbit models bring precision genetics to this species. #RabbitModels

Mice, rats, rabbits. The principles of genetic engineering apply across species. Transgenic models carrying foreign genes give researchers tools in the species most relevant to their work. #Transgenic
